text:
Priya (Support): customers on acct=ACME reporting huge p99 latency spike since ~09:20 UTC. Multiple API errors and long tail responses. raising here, tagging eng-oncall @Alex. sample req: req_id=0a3f4b2c, region=us-west-2.

Alex (Eng-Oncall): thanks @Priya. any repro curl or recent deploys? are we seeing alerts in paging?

Priya (Support): No customer-side deploys. They provided this curl trace (redacted token):
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer ***\" \n  -d '{"input":"..."}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
```
Response times: most requests ok, but p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~900ms, p99 ~450ms -> ~3.4s. Errors seen: 502 and 504 intermittently.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4527 - p99 latency spike (support).

Alex (Eng-Oncall): grabbing metrics. Jordan are you able to look at admission/backpressure graphs for us-west-2?

Jordan (Eng-SRE): looking now. I see a large surge of short-lived high-concurrency requests from a handful of IPs hitting the realtime route. Admission controller queue length spiked and workers started rejecting requests -> 503s. Overlayed memory pressure on a subset of workers. quick metrics:
- route: /v1/generate-realtime
- 08:50->09:20 UTC: tail QPS up 6x for that customer
- p95: 0.12s -> 0.92s
- p99: 0.45s -> 3.4s
- admission_queue_len: 20 -> 480
- worker_retries: +230

Jordan (Eng-SRE): snippet from runtime logs (truncated):
```
[2026-06-03T09:23:12Z] warn admission: enqueue drop=true len=472 max_concurrency=256 route=/v1/generate-realtime worker=dispatcher-7 req_id=0a3f4b2c
[2026-06-03T09:23:12Z] error worker: OOM candidate: model=redwood-13b-quant nodes=dispatcher-7 mem_used=93% fallback_invoked=false
```

Marta (Runtime): these dispatchers are pinned to model redwood-13b-quant and cannot spill over due to routing policy. We also have hot KV-cache thrashing with that customer pattern (many short random prefixes).

Alex (Eng-Oncall): any recent rollout to admission controller or autoscaler?

Jordan (Eng-SRE): no deploys in the last 6h. Autoscaler kept target steady; but burst capacity was exhausted because we have a per-account reserved quota that prevents instant scale for Dedicated accounts. This customer is hitting that cap.

Priya (Support): customer says they are running a throughput test. they expected throttling but not 5xxs. asking for mitigation now, they are blocked.

Marta (Runtime): quick mitigations we can try:
- route this tenant to the smaller model (redwood-7b) via routing override (fast to apply, reduces memory pressure)
- temporarily increase admission_controller.max_pending from 512 -> 1024 (risk: queueing increases latency for others)
- enable burst capacity in us-west-2 (if billing ops approves)
- add edge-rate-limit for this API key to throttle the spike (best customer-facing immediate fix)

Jordan (Eng-SRE): I recommend edge-rate-limit + routing override. we applied a soft rate-limit of 300 RPS for that API key at the CDN/edge at 09:30 UTC. also created routing override to redirect that key to redwood-7b-canary at 09:33 UTC.

Priya (Support): relayed to customer, they accepted temporary rate-limit and model downgrade.

Jordan (Eng-SRE): quick results: after edge limit + routing change:
- admission_queue_len dropped from 480 -> 30 within 2m
- p95 improved to ~220ms
- p99 improved to ~720ms (still elevated but much better)
- 5xxs dropped to near zero

Alex (Eng-Oncall): great. follow-up next steps?

Marta (Runtime): action items:
1) investigate KV-cache pattern and add cache hot keys mitigation (prefix bucketing) - assign to runtime team.
2) review per-account reserved quota and burst policy for Dedicated customers - assign to product/infra.
3) add per-API-key adaptive throttling (automated) to reduce manual ops.
4) add eval to detect bursty short-prefix patterns that cause thrashing.

Jordan (Eng-SRE): I'll keep this thread open for a postmortem. Ops-bot will create follow-up tasks.

ops-bot: Created task TASK-1049 (runtime: cache hotkey mitigation), TASK-1050 (product: burst capacity policy).

Priya (Support): customer confirmed they can proceed with reduced RPS for now. asked for ETA on permanent fix. I told them we'll follow up in 48h.

Alex (Eng-Oncall): marking incident INC-2026-4527 as mitigated. leaving monitor on for 24h. tagging: @Marta @Jordan for PM. :white_check_mark:

Jordan (Eng-SRE): note for postmortem - don't auto-increase admission_controller.max_pending without mem checks, routing overrides are safer. Also consider connection-level fairness to avoid single-tenant thrash.

Priya (Support): thanks team. I'll update the customer thread and close the support ticket once PMs confirm timeline. :pray:

Marta (Runtime): adding logs + sample req_ids to the postmortem doc: 0a3f4b2c, 4f8d9e11, 98abc123. link: https://redwood-internal/pm/incidents/INC-2026-4527

Alex (Eng-Oncall): good work. keeping this in \"incidents\" for 24h then move to postmortem.

(Reaction summary: :thumbsup: Alex, :eyes: Jordan, :white_check_mark: Priya)
